text:
mike: quick heads-up — noticed a latency/regression after landing AWQ profile for mixtral-8x. p95 increased ~18% on long seq runs (2k tokens) compared to our previous INT8 profile. logs + flame attached.
anya: ugh. is it happening on hot kernels or falling back to generic GEMM? :eyes:
mike: looks like kernel switch. profiler shows many steps hitting `matmul_fallback` during KV write/concat for heads=32 config. before it was using `fused_kv_matmul_sm90`.
li-wei: can you paste the perf diff? numbers?
mike: sure — short snippet from perf run:
```
model: mixtral-8x-awq
seq: 2048
batch: 1
p50: 210ms -> 247ms (+17.6%)
p95: 395ms -> 467ms (+18.2%)
tokens/s: 78 -> 64 (-17.9%)
hot kernel: matmul_fallback (40% time), kv_concat (22%), rotary_apply (12%)
```
mike: protobuf shows zero-point layout mismatch flagged during kernel select path for AWQ-packed weights. runtime fell back because `wei.layout != expected_layout`.
anya: hmm maybe AWQ packing uses per-head scales that change stride. could be RoPE scaling interplay? we changed rope_scale_factor for this model in the last PR.
josh: remind me — what head/kv dims are we using for mixtral-8x here? any nonstandard head split?
li-wei: mixtral-8x: d_model=8192, heads=64, kv_dim=128 (per-head). earlier we tested a heads=32 build for latency. for this run it's 64.
anya: RoPE scaling was increased to 1.1 for long-context stability. that changes the cos/sin precompute and can affect fused kernels if they assume certain stride packing.
mike: hypothesis: AWQ calibration reordered quant blocks (per-head) + rope_scale change -> packing layout mismatch -> runtime avoids optimized fused kernel -> fallback GEMM -> perf hit.
josh: we should bisect: (A) AWQ packing variant vs (B) GPTQ-style packing, and (C) original AWQ but revert rope_scale. also test heads=32 vs heads=64.
li-wei: I ran a quick micro-bench:
```
mixtral-awq + rope_scale=1.1 + heads=64 -> tokens/s 64
mixtral-awq + rope_scale=1.0 + heads=64 -> tokens/s 75
mixtral-gptq+rope_scale=1.1 + heads=64 -> tokens/s 73
mixtral-awq + rope_scale=1.1 + heads=32 -> tokens/s 82
```
li-wei: so rope_scale revert helps, and lowering heads reduces overhead (expected), but AWQ->GPTQ packing also restored most perf.
anya: interesting. accuracy delta between AWQ and GPTQ on our short eval was ~0.4% BLEU-like for QA prompts. acceptable? we need to check hallucination rates.
josh: also need to watch KV cache behavior — microbatch prefetch seems to thrash L2 when heads=64 with fallback kernel. maybe tweak batcher to prefer microbatching by sequence instead of tokens for these configs.
perf-bot: alert: canary job mixtral-8x-awq failed latency SLA at 2026-03-17T14:21:05Z. tag: perf-regression. Jira: INF-1423
mike: thanks perf-bot. plan: run a structured bisect today — script will toggle {packing: awq/gptq, rope_scale: 1.0/1.1, heads: 32/64} and collect p50/p95/tokens/s+kernel selection logs. also run calibration prompts for AWQ: short technical + conversational set.
josh: for calibration prompts, use the new mixed-calib set: 200 samples (50 instr, 50 conv, 50 code, 50 long-context). e.g., `calib_prompt_short = "In 2 sentences, explain Newton's second law."` and the long ones include >512 tokens doc snippets.
li-wei: I'll instrument kernel selector to dump `expected_layout` vs `wei.layout` on mismatch so we can map which packing flag differs.
anya: also try `allow_fp8=true` path for Mixtral to see if fp8 path uses different kernel that bypasses the fallback (may help perf but check accuracy).
mike: allocated 2h on ci-gpu-07 for the bisect. I'll post results here when done. if we confirm packing mismatch, we can either adapt kernel selector to accept the AWQ layout or change quantizer to emit compatible layout.
josh: if we adapt selector, add a cheap fast-path check so we don't regress kernel decision time.
li-wei: noted. I'll start with layout dumps and then run the two-packer bisect. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.
mike: thanks everyone. next update in ~2.5 hrs. :thumbsup:
